overview.heading: Six directions, one manipulator
body: This thesis extends the autonomy of the FHNW Mars Rover along six directions, centred on a language-conditioned manipulation policy and the software needed to train it, deploy it on board, and orchestrate it. The per-task models of the previous project are replaced by a single SmolVLA policy conditioned on a natural-language task description, post-trained with RECAP — an advantage-conditioned reinforcement-learning recipe — and compiled to TensorRT so it holds the control-cycle budget on the rover's Jetson Orin.

Around the policy sits a workflow layer: the open-source automation tool n8n, bridged to ROS 2 topics, services and actions, so an operator composes task sequences without writing code and an LLM agent can answer diagnostic questions by calling the same tools. Underneath it, a classical visual-servoing approach phase handles what language cannot disambiguate, and every autonomous controller actuates only behind an operator heartbeat and a latching software e-stop.
The report covers all of this in detail. This page is for the parts a PDF cannot hold: a rover you can send somewhere, workflows you can open, and a policy you can argue with.

contributions.title: Vision-language-action policies with reinforcement learning
contributions.body: A single SmolVLA policy conditioned on a natural-language task description replaces the per-task models of the previous project, then is post-trained with RECAP, an advantage-conditioned RL recipe.
contributions.question: RQ1 · task automation and reinforcement learning

contributions.title: Workflow automation and agentic control
contributions.body: n8n is integrated with ROS 2 over rosbridge, giving operators a no-code way to compose task sequences from topics, services and actions. An LLM agent calls the same tools to answer free-text diagnostic questions.

metric.label: finetuned to run on board
metric.note: trained on the agent's own recorded executions

contributions.question: RQ1 · task automation, RQ3 · safe handling of plan changes

contributions.title: Real-time deployment on the Jetson Orin
contributions.body: The policy is compiled to TensorRT, split into a VLM prefix and a flow-matching action expert. The prefix stays FP32 — converting the whole graph to FP16 collapses the policy's actions and is rejected by the numerical acceptance check.

metric.label: per chunk, ≈3 Hz replanning
metric.note: 428 ms with the full ten-step sampler; 2.6× over the uncompiled baseline

contributions.question: RQ1 · enabling work

contributions.title: Depth sensing
contributions.body: The time-of-flight grid in the gripper is routed into the policy's state input as an additional observation, through one configuration entry and with the policy itself unchanged. It buys a near-field measurement where no markers are available.

metric.label: in-gripper ToF grid
metric.note: state input, not a positioning method of its own

contributions.question: RQ2 · marker-free depth-based control

contributions.title: Visual servoing
contributions.body: "The third switch from the left" is five identical objects and a counting problem. Language does not disambiguate that, so the classical approach phase stays — reimplemented in C++ to hold its rate on board, and characterised end to end against the maintenance panel.

metric.label: tolerance, occluded target
metric.note: two defects fixed: fiducial pose ambiguity and a zeroed tool-axis offset

contributions.question: RQ2 · precise positioning

contributions.title: Manipulator control and safety gating
contributions.body: Per-joint weighting is added to the Cartesian solver, controlling how much each axis contributes to a motion. Every autonomous controller, learned or classical, actuates only behind an operator heartbeat and a latching software e-stop.

metric.label: of stopping
metric.note: hardware stop, latching software e-stop, heartbeat, cancellable phase actions

contributions.question: RQ3 · safe handling of errors and interruption

demos.title: A virtual rover, driven by n8n
demos.body: A simulated rover offering real ROS 2 topics, services and actions, driven by eleven n8n workflows — and a read-only live view anyone can open. Send it to the lake from your phone, watch the battery watchdog preempt a patrol, or ask the agent what interfaces the robot has.
points: Live view of the robot, read-only at the protocol level
All eleven workflows on a real n8n canvas
The n8n editor, the drive form, and the agent chat

demos.title: SmolVLA + RECAP + guidance, client-side
demos.body: The policy family from contribution 01, solving PushT entirely in the browser: Chipmunk2D physics as WASM, inference on WebGPU. Drag the agent away and watch the policy recover; move the guidance weight and watch what it does — and does not — change.
points: Take over from the policy mid-episode
Sampled action chunks drawn on the arena
Guidance weight and the denoising steps, both scrubable

figures.heading: Selected figures
figures.note: A handful of figures that read well on a screen. The report has the rest, with the argument around them.

items.alt: The deep-sampling workflow on the n8n canvas
items.caption: The deep-sampling workflow on the n8n canvas: the form trigger and the operator's container and mode selection on the left, then five phases — set parameters, drill, unload, tare, weigh. The branch at the bottom exposes the individual drill commands to the operator.

items.alt: The tool-change workflow on the n8n canvas
items.caption: The tool-change workflow. Joint state is read once on the left and replayed on the right, so the arm returns to the pose it started from. Labelled in German, as the team built it.

items.alt: The ROS 2 agent workflow in n8n
items.caption: The agent: plain tools, so it fills in every ROS name, type and payload itself. Nothing about the robot is hardcoded in the workflow.

items.alt: The ROS 2 node palette in n8n
items.caption: The node palette: topics, services, actions and the rosapi discovery node, all usable as agent tools.
